claim: rumqttc's eventloop does not re-subscribe after reconnection — the caller must re-send subscriptions after every ConnAck (issue #250, confirmed at source level in eventloop.rs)
note: 4 sources incl. crate source; ha-linux-agent violates this today (subscribes once at startup)

claim: rumqttc defaults to clean_session=true, which discards pending messages and subscriptions on every reconnect — a reliable agent needs clean_session=false + a stable client_id

A device exposing MQTT discovery must subscribe to Home Assistant's birth message (homeassistant/status, payload 'online') and re-publish its discovery payloads in response — HA's official documentation states this directly
LWT never fires on graceful disconnect — an agent must publish its own offline/shutdown message on SIGTERM before disconnecting (ESPHome shutdown_message, HASS.Agent, HiveMQ spec)
note: ha-linux-agent has no SIGTERM handler; the agent is killed and only the broker's LWT marks it offline

claim: MQTT discovery messages must be retained AND/OR republished on reconnect — retained state + availability are what make entities survive HA restarts; command topics must never be retained
note: 5 sources; ha-linux-agent retains state and discovery but never republishes

claim: Every discovery payload must include an availability topic (avty_t) or entities show unavailable/stuck states on integration restart
note: ha-linux-agent does include availability_topic — one thing it already gets right

claim: NixOS supports declarative per-user lingering via users.users.<name>.linger (23.11+, PR #260248); nixos-rebuild actively disables linger for users not declared in config
note: jupiter-os already sets users.users.io.linger in the ha-agent module

claim: User services cannot order themselves after system units, and the user-manager needs lingering to exist at boot on headless hosts — the session bus at /run/user/<uid>/bus only exists under a user manager
note: The headless diagnostic ladder: linger → XDG_RUNTIME_DIR → session bus → 'No medium found'

claim: Telegraf's MQTT output cannot produce Home Assistant discovery (homie layout only), cannot set a dynamic LWT, and has 'very limited' lifecycle management — it is not a substitute for a discovery-native agent
note: The Telegraf2Hassio community bridge exists precisely because of this gap

claim: HA's Prometheus integration is entity-export-only and cannot ingest host metrics from node_exporter — 'just use node_exporter with HA' is not a viable path

The Glances HA integration has a 6-year record of silent-failure modes (flatline without recovery #110551 2024 / #170384 2026-open, restart renames #32328, connect failures #2504) — pull-based per-host REST polling is an anti-pattern for fleet monitoring
Netdata's default footprint (1-5% of a core, 100-350MB RAM) is too heavy for fleet-wide kiosk deployment without explicit tuning; its memory blowups are community-documented
note: Disqualifies 'adopt Netdata everywhere' for TCxWave-class hardware

claim: The Windows companion HASS.Agent explicitly does not target Linux, and no official Linux companion exists — the niche ha-linux-agent occupies is genuinely open (community demand documented in the WTH thread)

tailscale status --json's BackendState / Self / TailscaleIPs / ExitNodeStatus fields are authoritatively defined in tailscale.com/ipn/ipnstate Go structs, but the --json format is officially unstable-by-policy — an agent parsing it must version-tolerate
note: Closes the ROADMAP's 'schema not pinned down' hesitation — the fields exist and are known, with a stability caveat

claim: MQTT integration tests need a real ephemeral broker (Mosquitto testcontainer) with the broker URL derived from the container API, never hardcoded localhost:1883
note: Direct remediation path for the 3-tests-in-12-crates gap
